title: Recite what is easy
hook: He knows you can't keep it all, so recite what is easy for you (73:20)

segments.voice: Yesterday: tartil, slow and measured recitation, and your line, slowly, measured. Today, the last verse of al-Muzzammil, and it changes the rules.

Some resolutions are too big to keep. Run every morning. Read for an hour a day. Never check the phone after nine. Two weeks in, the whole plan collapses. Surah al-Muzzammil began with a huge ask: stand half the night in prayer, sometimes more. And the Prophet and some of those with him tried, night after night. Then the surah's last verse arrives, much longer than the others, and it says something that sounds almost like relief.

Verse twenty speaks straight to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: your Lord knows that you stand nearly two thirds of the night, or half, or a third, and so do some of those with you. He knows you can't keep count of it all, so He has turned to you in mercy. Then: recite of the Qur'an what is easy for you. And it names why. Some of you will be sick. Some will be traveling the land, seeking a living. Some will be fighting in the cause of Allah. The verse knows people's lives, illness, work trips, hard duties, and doesn't pretend they don't exist. A hadith in Sahih Muslim, from 'A'ishah, gives the history. When the surah began, she said, night prayer was made obligatory, and the Prophet and his companions kept it for a year. Allah held back the end of the surah for twelve months, then revealed this lightening, and the night prayer became voluntary. Notice what didn't change. The verse doesn't say forget it. It says recite what is easy. The practice stays; its size changes. And it adds the things that keep going no matter what: establish the prayer, give the zakat, lend Allah a good loan, ask His forgiveness. A hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari sits beside this verse: the religion is easy, and whoever makes it too hard will be overcome by it. The surah doesn't lower the bar to zero. It sets it where a real person can keep stepping over it.
screen: `HE KNOWS YOU CAN'T KEEP IT ALL.`

segments.voice: Think of one good habit you dropped because it got too big: prayer, reading, exercise, calling someone you love. Shrink it until it's easy, one verse instead of a page, one minute instead of thirty, small enough that you'd be embarrassed not to do it. Then decide where it fits in your day.
Al-Muzzammil, the surah that began with a huge ask, half the night in prayer, before its last verse lightens it: recite what is easy. Today's word.
Your line: what is easy. Easy is not the same as nothing at all. Day six hundred fifty-four.

howItsDone: Night prayer (tahajjud) is held to be voluntary for the community; some Muslims keep a small, steady portion of it, or a daily portion of Qur'an recitation, following 73:20 and the hadith that the religion is easy.

original.note: Arabic, 73:20: so recite what is easy of the Qur'an.

trapdoor: what you thought: you can do less if you want.
what it means: the heavy night vigil is lightened for real lives, but recitation, prayer and giving continue.
what a scholar hears: 'A'ishah's report in Muslim says a year passed between the surah's opening and 73:20; the lightening is read as making night prayer voluntary.

chat.says: Did the long night prayer in al-Muzzammil stay required for everyone?
options: No; after a year, 73:20 lightened it to what is easy, and it became voluntary.
Yes; everyone must still stand half of every night, without exception.
No; it was dropped completely, so night prayer has no place anymore.
chat.meaning: 'A'ishah said night prayer was obligatory for a year, then 73:20 came: recite what is easy. The practice stayed; its size changed.

'A'ishah.meaning: the Prophet's wife, who gives the history
